BERT4Rec’s random-mask reconstruction differs from terminal-mask recommendation; recency-sampling research explicitly identifies weak alignment between masking and next-item prediction. Proposed inexpensive probe: on the same training histories, compute separate interior-mask and terminal-mask losses, gradient norms, and gradient cosine similarity for item embeddings, positional embeddings, attention and output layers. Negative cosine indicates local objective conflict, following [PCGrad](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782); it does not establish worse generalization. Keep targets hidden and read the final nonpadding mask. Sources: [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), [recency sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643).

For popularity shortcuts, proposed interventions on the existing checkpoint: remove any output bias, zero positional activations, shuffle only observed history items, and replace histories with length-matched controls. Measure paired changes in target margins, loss and recommendation overlap; stratify by training-frequency and history length. Report normalized gradient magnitudes alongside activation interventions: small gradients alone cannot distinguish irrelevance from saturation. Order shuffling tests order dependence; positional ablation tests dependence on positional inputs. Neither alone proves useful temporal learning. These are diagnostic proposals, not established BERT4Rec findings from the search.

[Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03292) and its [2024 reassessment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.02383) motivate checking attribution sensitivity to parameter randomization. Temporarily randomize selected layers, compare attribution changes, then restore weights exactly; include random-position perturbation controls. Separate training-exposed sensitivity from held-out validation effects, with uncertainty across users. Use one checkpoint per category, reversible interventions and no fitted auxiliary scorer; accept changes only through the fixed macro validation HR@10.
